comment: Self-exchange rate constants (RedoxCouple.k_self, M-1 s-1) of couples that move an oxygen atom. A couple whose two forms differ by electrons only (I2 / I-, Cl2 / Cl-, Hg2+2 / Hg+2) needs no row: the structure says so (gem/redox.rs is_electron_transfer_couple). A couple of an element that is not in redox_lability.json, whose forms differ in composition, is inert on bench time unless a row here (or a registered kinetic row) says otherwise: thermodynamics decides whether a reaction is allowed, never that a kinetically hindered couple reacts. The rows are the oxo-transfer couples whose reduced or oxidised end is kinetically *reactive* (the O-O bond of a peroxide, the weak X-O bond of a hypohalite, the lone pair of sulfite and nitrite), as opposed to the inert ends (sulfate, nitrate, perchlorate, O2, N2). The value is an effective Marcus self-exchange rate: oxo transfer is not outer-sphere electron transfer and has no measurable self-exchange, so each value is fitted once, with the cross relation of gem/rates.rs, to the order of magnitude of one measured rate of the couple with a reference partner (see 'fit'); the cross relation then carries it to every other partner by its driving force. Tier Speculative. Species that the store does not hold are skipped. OUTER-SPHERE ROWS (kind outer_sphere_measured): the self-exchange constants are attributed to the cited papers and to Marcus & Sutin, Biochim. Biophys. Acta 811, 265 (1985), but were written from memory and NOT checked against them (verification recalled, tier Estimated, not Tabulated; none of the cited tables and pages was opened). The couples I2 / I- and Br2 / Br- are not outer-sphere transfers at all and their rows are placeholders of the right order of magnitude.

couples.source: effective self-exchange of the O-O bond reduction H2O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> 2 H2O (E0 1.776 V, NBS / CRC)
couples.fit: H2O2 + I- (uncatalysed path): 0.0115 M-1 s-1 at 25 C (Liebhafsky & Mohammad 1933), recalled

couples.source: effective self-exchange of the O-O bond reduction S2O8-2 + 2e- -> 2 SO4-2 (E0 2.01 V)
couples.fit: S2O8-2 + I-: 0.03 M-1 s-1 at 25 C (the registered kinetic row of the iodine clock, Indelli & Prue 1958); the cross relation carries it to Fe(II), thiosulfate, sulfite and the rest

couples.source: effective self-exchange of the X-O bond reduction HOCl + H+ + 2e- -> Cl- + H2O (E0 1.482 V)
couples.fit: OCl- + I- at pH 10: of the order of 1e1-1e3 M-1 s-1 (hypochlorite oxidises iodide at once at bench concentrations; the reaction is a nucleophilic attack of I- on the O-Cl bond, which the electron-transfer cross relation can only mimic with a large effective self-exchange rate), recalled

couples.source: effective self-exchange of the X-O bond reduction HOBr + H+ + 2e- -> Br- + H2O (E0 1.33 V); same class as hypochlorite
effective self-exchange of the oxidation of sulfur(IV) to sulfur(VI) by oxygen-atom transfer from water (E0 0.172 V, SO4-2 / H2SO3)
couples.fit: sulfite with a strong oxidant (permanganate, dichromate, iodine, Fe(III)): fast on the bench, 1e3 M-1 s-1 and more, recalled order of magnitude

couples.source: effective self-exchange of the oxidation of nitrite to nitrate by oxygen-atom transfer from water (E0 0.94 V, NO3- / HNO2)
couples.fit: nitrite with permanganate in acid: of the order of 1e1 M-1 s-1, recalled
